<!-- pr-reviewer: 61e0f593e721c3df9f216800301ea86ae05b0ce4 -->
Reviewer: m3 pool job review-4119 (config `.claude-team2`), claude-opus-5-5, mkinney; did not write or refresh this PR.

**Needs changes before merge.** The tests do not pin two union rules of the collision body, and the default shank position puts a library holder too far from the tip.

Scope of this review: the spindle slice of #3643 (`f2eedafa0`, and the merge `61e0f593e`). The #4096 commits on this branch are reviewed on #4096. That PR has `needs-rework` on an older head, and its current head `d36523d9d` waits for a review. This PR merges only after #4096 merges (stack rule in AGENTS.md).

Tier: high. The slice makes the `HolderProfile` that the collision laws will read. No caller reads it yet, so no posted G-code, no simulation and no current collision check changes.

## What looks good

- Pure domain code in `camcraft-tools`. No new crate edge, no ECS, no file I/O. Each new module has a provenance line. Each file is under 400 lines.
- No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` outside tests. Each index comes from a checked parent or from `enumerate`.
- `Frame::new` refuses non-finite and degenerate frames by name. Cycles, bad parents, two roots, two cutters, ambiguous and taken ports are refused by name.
- The equivalence pins against `HolderRef` are a good design: the one-body path is the same shape that the laws read today.
- The flute check and the stickout rules are pinned (mutations below).

## Results (locally, on a trial merge with upstream/main `0604494bc`, macOS)

- Trial merge: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 1 step, `tools suites: lib`: 173 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Light lane (`cargo xtask gate light`): not run by this review. The 6 light twins are in `motion` and `app`, and the new modules have no caller. The author reports 6 of 6 ok on `f2eedafa0`. This is not a pass from this review.
- Extra suites run: none apply. The diff changes no `testdata/`, no fixture and no importer code.
- Goldens moved: none. No `*.nc`, `*.cl` or catalog file changed.

## Mutations (`cargo test -p camcraft-tools --lib tool_assembly`)

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| `union`: overlap takes `f64::min`, not `f64::max` (`tool_assembly_body.rs:107`) | **survives** (8 passed) |
| `union`: a gap between two bodies gets radius `0.0`, not the smaller neighbour (`tool_assembly_body.rs:117`) | **survives** (8 passed) |
| `union`: a gap gets the larger neighbour | survives (harmless: larger only) |
| flute check removed (`tool_assembly_body.rs:87`) | caught by `bodies_in_the_flutes_and_bad_stickouts_are_refused_by_name` |
| insert diameter `r`, not `2r` (`tool_assembly_body.rs:49`) | caught by `an_indexable_cutter_takes_its_diameter_and_corner_from_seat_and_insert` |
| stickout shift with the wrong sign (`tool_assembly.rs:251`) | caught by 3 tests |

## Requested before merge

1. **The union rules of the judged body are not pinned** (`crates/tools/src/tool_assembly_body.rs:99-122`). Class: each rule that keeps the envelope "never smaller" needs a test that fails when the rule is wrong.
   - The "larger radius wins" rule is the rule that matters for a collet chuck. A collet body sits inside the chuck nose, so the two bodies overlap. With `f64::min`, the collet radius replaces the chuck radius, and the envelope becomes smaller than the chuck. All tests still pass.
   - The gap rule (the smaller neighbour) can become `0.0` and all tests still pass.
   - No test has two bodies that overlap or two bodies with a gap. The stack-up test has two bodies that only touch. The collet test has a collet with no body.
   - Fix: add one test with an overlap (for example, an ER collet body inside the chuck nose) and one test with a gap. Assert the bands. The two mutations above must then fail.

2. **The default shank position ("fully home") puts the tool entirely out of a library holder** (`crates/tools/src/tool_assembly.rs:249-251`, `crates/tools/src/component_geometry.rs:105-114`, `crates/tools/src/tool_assembly_tests.rs:112-128`).
   - `ComponentGeometry::holder` puts the one port on the nose face. With `projection_mm: None`, the shank back end (the tool MCS) sits on that port. Thus the whole tool hangs below the nose face, with no shank in the bore.
   - The explicit path refuses this exact state. `stickout_shift` refuses `p >= tip` with "the stickout leaves no shank in the bore". The default gives `p == tip` and is accepted.
   - The Weldon pin calls this state "the shank fully home" and asserts `gauge_len == len + entry.gauge_len` (line 125). A real Weldon shank sits in the bore up to its stop. The real stickout is shorter than `len` by the insertion depth.
   - Effect when #3644 connects the resolver: the gauge length is too long by the insertion depth. The holder body is modelled that distance higher above the tip than the real holder. A holder collision can then pass the check.
   - Class: a shank's default position must come from a stated stop (a bore-bottom port frame or a bore depth), never from the nose face. Fix one of these two ways:
     - Refuse `projection_mm: None` for a solid tool on a plain or Weldon bore when the geometry does not state the stop.
     - Give `ComponentGeometry::holder` (or the geometry) the bore depth, and put the "home" position there.
   - Then pin the Weldon equivalence at the true stickout, not at `len`. Correct the decision file (`docs/decisions/3643-tool-assemblies.md`, the `projection_mm` bullet).

## Optional, non-blocking

- `docs/decisions/3643-tool-assemblies.md`, indexable cutter bullet: "a smaller corner radius never makes the model larger than the real tool" says the opposite of the effect. A sharp corner (0) gives a model that is larger at the corner than a chamfered or radiused real tool. The choice is safe for a gouge check, but the text is inverted.
- `crates/tools/src/tool_assembly.rs:114`: `to_tool` names `nodes[0]` in a `BadFrame` refusal, not the node that failed. The refusal cannot occur after the gauge cap, so this is only a wording point.
- `crates/tools/src/tool_assembly_body.rs:83`: `SpunProfile::from_bands(...)` drops its error with `Option`. This is only the display outline, and the judged `profile` is kept. A log line or a comment would help.

The PR waits for the fixes above and for #4096. A collaborator session merges it at the cut (`feat`).

Fixes for the review on `61e0f593e` (comment 7184474248). Commit `808743798` closes the two findings and the three optional points. The new head waits for a fresh review.

## Finding 1: the union rules of the judged body

Class: each rule that keeps the envelope "never smaller" needs a test that fails when the rule is wrong.

- New test `overlapping_bodies_keep_the_larger_radius`. An ER collet body reaches 20 mm up into the chuck nose. The test asserts the radius below the nose (collet), in the overlap (chuck) and above it (chuck).
- New test `a_gap_between_bodies_takes_the_smaller_neighbour`. Two bodies have a 30 mm span between them with no body. The test asserts that the span takes the smaller neighbour radius.
- Mutation results (`cargo test -p camcraft-tools --lib tool_assembly`, applied, run, reverted):
  - overlap takes `f64::min`: caught, `overlapping_bodies_keep_the_larger_radius` fails.
  - a gap gets radius `0.0`: caught, `a_gap_between_bodies_takes_the_smaller_neighbour` fails.
  - base (no mutation): 11 passed.

## Finding 2: the default shank position

Class rule: a shank has a home position only on a stated stop. The nose face is never a home position.

- The library entries (`holder_library`) have no bore depth and no clamping length. Thus there is no real stop to use, and the resolver refuses.
- `ComponentGeometry::with_stop(port, depth)` states a bore stop: the depth from the port frame to the stop, along the port's +Z.
- A solid tool on a plain or Weldon bore with `projection_mm: None` sits home on the stated stop. Without a stated stop it is refused by name ("the holder states no bore stop, so the shank has no home position: state a stickout").
- A stop that is as deep as the tool is long is refused.
- A stated stickout that pushes the shank past a stated stop is refused.
- `ComponentGeometry::holder` states no stop. Thus a solid tool in a library holder needs a stated stickout.
- The Weldon equivalence pin now runs at the true stickout: the tool length less the stop depth. The shank home on the stop and the same stickout stated both give the gauge length and the bands of `HolderRef` at that stickout.
- New test `a_shank_with_no_stated_stop_or_past_its_stop_is_refused` pins each refusal, a legal shallower shank, and the `with_stop` refusals (unknown port, depth 0, below 0, NaN).
- `an_off_axis_body_and_degenerate_geometry_are_refused_by_name` now states a stickout, because its shank mount had no stop.
- The `projection_mm` bullet of `docs/decisions/3643-tool-assemblies.md` states the stop rule and why the nose face is not a stop.
- Mutation results:
  - the shank sits on the nose face when no stop is stated (the old default): caught, `a_shank_with_no_stated_stop_or_past_its_stop_is_refused` fails.
  - the past-the-stop check removed: caught, the same test fails.

## Optional points

- The decision file: the corner radius sentence now says that a sharp corner makes the model larger than the real tool at the corner, which is the safe side for a gouge check.
- `to_tool` names the node whose frame fails (and the cutting item for the cutting point), not `nodes[0]`.
- `tool_assembly_body.rs`: a comment says that a dropped `SpunProfile::from_bands` error removes only the display outline, and that the judged `profile` stays.

## Gate on `808743798` (winbuild, Windows)

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: one step, `tools suites: lib`: 176 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Light lane: not run. The fixes change only `camcraft-tools` lib code and the decision file.

Ready for a re-check.

Reviewer: wopr pool job review-4119, GPT-6 (Codex), mkinney; did not write or refresh this PR.

Clean review. No blocking findings. The PR is MERGEABLE.

Previous findings checked:

1. **Body union tests: fixed in `808743798`.** `overlapping_bodies_keep_the_larger_radius` checks the collet, the overlap, and the chuck. `a_gap_between_bodies_takes_the_smaller_neighbour` checks the gap and both adjacent bodies. Both tests pass. Both mutations that survived the earlier review now fail in these tests.
2. **Default shank position: fixed in `808743798`.** `home_shift` refuses a solid shank on a plain or Weldon bore without a stated stop. `with_stop` checks the port and the depth. A stated stickout cannot push the shank past the stop. The Weldon equivalence test uses the true stickout and checks both mounting paths against `HolderRef`. The refusal test passes. Both shank mutations fail in that test. The decision record states the corrected rule.
3. **Optional corner-radius wording: fixed.** The decision record now explains why a sharp model corner is conservative.
4. **Optional frame diagnostic: fixed.** `to_tool` names the affected node and uses the cutting node for the cutting point.
5. **Optional display outline comment: fixed.** The comment explains that the judged profile remains when the display outline cannot be made.

These results agree with the [author's reply](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/4119#issuecomment-7185027682). No new blocker was found in the fixes or the trial merge.

Scope and laws:

- This re-review checks the spindle assembly slice and its fixes. The inherited component work has a [clean review on #4096](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/4096#issuecomment-7185146075).
- The code stays in `camcraft-tools`. It adds no dependency, ECS access, project storage, or user command. The new modules state their provenance.
- Tier: SAFETY. The new resolver constructs tool geometry and a holder collision envelope. It has no production caller yet. Current posted G-code, simulation, and collision checks do not change.
- The review uses upstream/main's current `AGENTS.md`. The partial issue reference `Refs #3643` agrees with the remaining work listed in the body.

Local build and tests:

- Host: `wopr`, Linux. No GitHub runner was used. `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and `CLAUDE_JOB_DIR` are unset; the job identifier above names this review task.
- PR head: `8087437988b32fe132db75307a580c3d4621efc0`.
- Base: upstream/main `bd467a0ccf581f3f700209247b62e6949ab7735e`.
- Trial merge: `ea3fc36fa25bc79fbdeb5ece7d51e47c5d238d26`. Its first parent is the PR head. The merge was clean.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: passed. `tools suites: lib`: 176 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-tools --no-run`: passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-tools --lib tool_assembly`, after all mutations were restored: 11 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: all six steps passed, 0 failed, 0 stalled. These were the release build, motion lib, `adaptive_troch_island`, `adaptive_troch_neck`, `adaptive_troch_parallel`, and app `pocket_pass_start`.
- The compile cache reported a server warning and fell back to local compilation. The commands completed successfully.

Extra suites run: none beyond the quick gate, assembly tests, and light lane. No fixture, importer, post, operation, motion, or catalog file changed. Thus, the additional fixture, kernel STEP, machining mesh, feature-edge, and example catalog suites do not apply.

Mutations run locally with `cargo test -p camcraft-tools --lib tool_assembly`:

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| Overlap radius uses `f64::min` | RED: `overlapping_bodies_keep_the_larger_radius` fails; 10 pass, 1 fails. |
| Gap radius uses `0.0` | RED: `a_gap_between_bodies_takes_the_smaller_neighbour` fails; 10 pass, 1 fails. |
| A shank without a stop sits on the nose face | RED: `a_shank_with_no_stated_stop_or_past_its_stop_is_refused` fails; 10 pass, 1 fails. |
| The past-the-stop check is disabled | RED: the same shank refusal test fails; 10 pass, 1 fails. |
| Restored source | GREEN: all 11 assembly tests pass. |

Each mutation was restored before the next one. The final worktree has no tracked changes.

Goldens moved: none. No recorded program changed. No UI file changed, so screenshots are not required. No full heavy lane was required or run.

Requested before merge: none. The PR follows #4096 in merge order and keeps the feature cut rule. The current head has no NeoTech change request. The earlier `needs-rework` label was set by mkinney on the previous head. The reviews API and comments were checked again before posting.

Set `merge-ready` and remove the earlier `needs-rework` label. Keep the review worktree and branch for the next round. The author is qsmits; this review leaves the PR's ready state unchanged.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
